messages.author: 51368d49cf7af539
messages.subject: Exponential Prior for GMRF parameters
parts:
I have a question regarding the choice of priors in general for the GMRF parameters (r,σ_u,σ_e) in [https://arxiv.org/pdf/1608.03787.pdf] in particular.

The above mentioned paper says in Section 0.2.2:
 The exponential distribution is a reasonable prior due to its memoryless property, which represents the idea that additional randomness should be penalized in the same way, independent of how much randomness you have already included in the model.

I do not quite understand this argument. Could someone explain to me what is meant by that?
I understand that the memoryless property of an exponential distribution X~Exp(lambda) says that Pr(X>s+t | X>s ) = Pr( X > t ). How is that related to the "randomness" mentioned above and the GMRF parameters?

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Exponential Prior for GMRF parameters
parts:
Hi,

This appendix is written from the perspective of dividing the total randomness or variation of the data into
- likelihood randomness (iid, cannot be "modelled")
- spatial randomness (spatial random effect)
- structured randomness (fixed effects etc)

You can think of it as decomposing a signal into modelled randomness and residuals.

The idea presented here is that the amount of "randomness" (or variation) you want to include in the spatial term should have the same penalty no matter how much you have "already included".

Best,
Haakon

does the "already included" refer to all (r,σ_u,σ_e) whose prior I assume to be exponential? Or what is explicitly meant by that (what are those other sources that could lead to variation in the spatial model)?

https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ss/1491465621
